items.q: What does Hu wish he had done faster, and what was the real cost?
items.a: The **drone → EV** cut. Not the slide. **People, cells, and momentum** felt like DNA. 'The biggest risk is you are letting go of something.' Attachment, not strategy, made the pivot late.

items.q: What did A123 do wrong, in Hu's telling?
items.a: LFP **too early** vs NCM. Then a **hired CEO** plus government money: 5,000 hires in 3 months, Michigan plant, tab-welding defects to GM, lost the contract to LG, **revenue at negative margin**. Bankrupt 2012. Founder CEO stays on the tech baby; professional CEO can forget who they are.

items.q: How did SES use A123 after the bankruptcy?
items.a: Walked into the emptied **Waltham** R&D line (peak ~200 → ~8 people), asked an engineer to run the **18650** line, built prototypes **for free**. Dead competitor as Series A lab. He says no other US battery company did that.

items.q: When the market is hot, what does Hu raise and what does he refuse to buy?
items.a: **Raise as much cash as you can** (SPAC 2021–22). Do **not** spend it on CapEx. Peers built prettier California plants and shut them. $100 of CapEx later sells for **less than a cent**. Skip listed-company theatre that does not serve the cell.

items.q: What challenge does he hate most, and what is the fix?
items.a: A **bad board** — ignorant, on an exit clock, or under LP pressure. Brand-name dollar = no-name dollar. Write **CEO vs board power**. 'If you don't give me the power, don't make me the CEO — make someone else the COO.' Pivots need concentrated power.

items.q: What is the AI bet, and how does he treat failure?
items.a: One year of field data + a model instead of **ten years** of EV qualification. AI for science, manufacturing, and safety; [[nvidia]] as compute partner. Success and failure are **labels on temporary states**. Costs are real. 'I'm a robot.'
